issues.detail: The condition `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` reads fine but the `typeof === 'undefined'` form is verbose. In this codebase PostCSS at-rules either have `.nodes` (block) or don't (statement). A direct check like `node.nodes == null` or `node.nodes !== undefined` is shorter and reads the same. Not a blocker; the patch is one line and obviously correct.

issues.description: Test only covers empty layer block; add a non-empty block case for completeness
issues.detail: The new test uses `@layer foo {}` — an empty block. The fix keys off `node.nodes` being defined, which is also true for non-empty blocks, so behavior is identical. Still, a test like `@layer foo { .x {} }` would document intent and guard against a future refactor that distinguishes empty vs non-empty nodes arrays. Minor.

review.summary: One-line fix to a real bug: `@layer foo {}` (layer block) before `@import` was being treated like a statement-form `@layer foo;` and silently skipped. The patch correctly distinguishes the two by checking whether the at-rule has a `.nodes` array. Diff is tight, scoped, matches surrounding style, ships with a test and a changeset. GOOD-TASTE-adjacent — eliminates a false negative by reading what the node actually is rather than adding a separate code path. ACCEPT, with optional nits on the `typeof` idiom and a non-empty-block test for future-proofing.
